Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

sure adjective

also certain, for sure, are you sure?, make sure, positive, I bet, I bet you’re tired

classical

Ter. Ad. 329: Satin' hoc certum est? — Certum.
Cic. Att. 2.19.5: certī sumus perīsse omnia
Traupman 108, 388

certus, certa, certum

sure, certain

Of a thing, certum est, it is certain; of a person, certus sum with an accusative and infinitive, I am sure that (Cicero, of bad news). But certum est mihi with an infinitive is “I have decided” (see decide), and certior fierī is “be told, be informed”.

Other words

  • certō (certum) sciō — I’m sure, I know for certain

    phrase: adverb with sciō · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 110: certum nōn scīmus; Traupman 95, 102

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs)

    Lewis & Short: the adverb certō is found only in comedy and in Cicero, most often in his letters; certē, certainly, belongs to every period.

  • prō certō habēre — take as certain, be sure of

    phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 10.6.3 (Lewis & Short, s.v. habeō); Traupman 95

  • fac (ut) — make sure (that) …, be sure to …

    phrase: imperative of faciō, with the subjunctive · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 16.18.3: fac ut sciam; Traupman 108, 388: fac modo ut veniās

    Also cūrā ut, as in Cicero’s sign-off cūrā ut valeās.

Examples

  • Satin' hoc certum est? — Certum: hīsce oculīs egomet vīdī.

    Is that quite certain? — Certain: I saw it with these very eyes.Ter. Ad. 329

  • Cīvemne? — Arbitror: certum nōn scīmus.

    A citizen? — I think so; we don’t know for sure.Ter. Eun. 110

  • tē quandō exspectēmus fac ut sciam

    make sure you let me know when to expect youCic. Fam. 16.18.3

See also certain, know, decide, of course.
